findings.title: Call to non-existent no-argument `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` breaks compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only inherited method is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`. There is no zero-argument overload, so this file cannot compile. Pass `context.getUser()` or add an overload before merge.

findings.title: Passkeys conditional UI no longer rendered when the user is not already set
findings.body: The new guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires a non-null user because `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` returns false when `user == null`. Previously this setup ran when `context.getUser() == null` to support first-factor username/password login with discoverable passkeys. The same inverted condition is used in the error challenge at line 137, so after an invalid username or empty-password error, where the context user is still null, the WebAuthn form is also lost. This breaks passkey auto-login and leaves the conditional webauthn form absent on the initial username/password page; tests that assert `//form[@id='webauth']` on that page will fail.
